: ABSTRACT « - . oe . . -
. This Aklanon-English dictionary consists of a list of
. basic root words or word’ bases of Aklanon. The dictionary is designed.
to be used both by native speakers of Aklanon and by fereign ros .
. learners. For the former, it can serve to: (1) establish a unifora °
- system of spelling, (2) broaden or intensify the use and.
. understanding of idiomatic standard American English, (3) serve as a .
‘ ceference book for the. standard speech of Kalibo, (4) broaden the .. .
. ‘wocabulary of those interested in studying their native language, and’ oy
(5) introduée a more linguistically oriented study of Aklanon. For
foreign, learners, it is useful as a language learning‘tool. The ve
. dictionary is preceded by a discussion of root words and their
derivations, an outline of the six basic grammatical functions and
. the basic parts,of speech of Aklanon, a discussion of -morphophonesic '
‘change,- and an explanation of the ‘conventions for spelling the . ae
* .* AKlanon dialect. A short bibliography of relevant references follows . .
the dictionary.« (CLR) . ; . .

This present book is the result of four years of painstaking research and re-edition. : *,
A If is a companion and follow-up volume to the GRAMMAR, published a year ago; but it _
te far more necessary and practical than its companion, volume. ,
, FOR AKLANONS it can serve the following functions: ; . oe ‘ \
(1) to establish a uniform system of spelling throughout the province; \
(2) to broaden oe intensify the use and understanding of idiomatic stan- \
dard American English, particularily for students and teachers; ’ {
(3) ‘to serve as a reference book for the standard speech [including bor- |
4 . rowed-and adopted terms] . of Kalibo--the. geographical, educational, . |
financial, mercantile and political center of the.province of Aklan; - . 7 Te
. (4) ‘to broaden the vocabulary and knowledge of those interested in
‘ _ studying their own dative dialect, since not only common, but also
. -. "deep" and foreign words are included as:they are actually used;
(5) to introduce a more linguistically oriented study of the Aklanon
language in order to break off from a long-standing tradition of "folk
linguistics" and so-called "dialect expetts". :
4 , ~ 5 " fe
FOR FOREIGN LEARNERS [whethtr. Western or other Filipinos} {t has the follow-
ing uses: . . . ; . ‘
(1) to help in translating the words of the.dialect into the more reach- ./
able idiom of English; ; mt
(2) to indicate the actual use of root words as they occur in curfent 778,
Aklanon speech; ; ott _ ,
. (3) to act as a pronunciation guide, since. accents'‘and phonemig¢ spellings ‘
, . [with some exceptions] are indicated; - . e .
co (4) to serve’as a list of the most Common and several uncommon words —_
which could be memorized from,time to time. ; ; ‘
FOR LINGUISTS we hope to provide another humble treatment of a hitherto unre-
searched language and enrich the catalog of literature available on the less known dia~-
.  lects and languages of the world. In addition, the word list contained herein should be ‘
of interest to etymologists as they will note the large‘number of reflexes or words re-
lated to other Philippine dialects and languages. Se 7
. Neither this dictionary nor its authors purport to have gathered evety word inthe ° ;
‘ Aklanion lahguage, but a major number are certainly represented. Native ¢peakers who |
« may browse through this book will be surprised at seeing x very large representation of
English and Spanish words. Some may be tempted to criticize their presence here: How-
ever, one need only eavesdrop on any conversation of local people--be-it formal or
informal--and hear for himself the overwhelming number of borrowed terms in actual . .
use. The authors have operatea on the principle that the sounds floating in.Aklanon air, .
. make up the total part and parcel of Aklanon sp ech, and should be represented here. .
| ‘ For those who will be startled to see al foreign or vulgar words we ask their.
‘| forbearance and understanding in this matter. ee 7 . |

. Uy INTRODUCTION -- HOW TO UNDERSTAND AND USE THIS DICTIONARY oe
This dictionary is a list of the basic root words or word bases of the Aklanon dia- a ,
lect (considered a language by linguists). , If one only wishes to get the general mean-
_ ing of words it should be relatively simple to use. However, if the reader wishes to ;
° . , reap the full fruit of all the information contained herein, such as how particular roots ‘
are used, or how they can grow into other parts of speech, we urge him to master the '
. grammatical explanations which will follow this section. :
